newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal minister sees no civil service dismissals.
newsitem.headline: Portugal minister sees no civil service dismissals.

text.p: Portuguese Employment Minister Maria Joao Rodrigues said the Socialist government did not plan to lay off any civil servants and that the number of public servants would not increase.
"I don't think there will be dismissals but the level of employment in the civil service will not increase," Rodrigues told Reuters in an interview on Friday night.
"The objective is to have more well-qualified public servants," she added.

Arnaldo Silva, the government's number two public sector wage negotiator, told Reuters last September that the government had no plans to reduce the size of the civil service, which he said was no more swollen than the European average. Portugal has an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 civil servants.

The government was studying reforms to the present inefficient distribution of civil servants across the ministries and was seeking to end the "precarious" freelance contracts regulating up to 10 percent of civil servants, Silva said.
